title: Pool-reused bombs flash red at placement — pulse phase from Date.now() makes fresh bombs look ready-to-explode
summary: User report: 'I noticed a bug — if you place a bomb (probably from a pool), if it's not the first, it's already red like ready to explode'. Reproduced live. Root cause: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/bomb-fuse-system.ts:44-66` (`bombPulseColor`) pulses the bomb mesh between #2a2a2a (grey) and #ff5a2a (warm orange) on a triangle-wave whose phase is `(Date.now() / 1000) % period / period`. Period scales with fuse (calmer at fresh, faster as fuse drops) but the *amplitude* always reaches full orange. Fresh bombs that happen to be placed when the global pulse phase is near the orange peak appear immediately bright red, indistinguishable from a bomb about to detonate. The S196 PR body promised 'lerps to hot orange in final 0.6s' — the actual implementation pulses orange at ALL fuse values. Live evidence: probe-driven place-bomb, polled every 250ms; first poll showed `bomb.player.1.2 fuse=1.92 color=#eb562a` — orange-red at a fuse with 76% remaining. Not a pool reuse bug per se (bomb-placement-system.ts:139 explicitly resets `MeshRenderer.color` to `#1a1a1a` on each spawn) — bomb-fuse-system overrides on the very next frame using the global pulse phase. User's pool theory is correct in spirit: subsequent bombs DO inherit a 'wrong' state, just not literally from the pool — they inherit the global pulse phase that's been ticking the whole time.
repro: Set BomberStats `maxBombs:5` on player.1 via POST `/__agf/component/player.1/BomberStats`.
Poll `/__agf/snapshot` every 250 ms for ~4 s; track the bomb entity's `MeshRenderer.color`.
Observe: even at fuse=1.92 (76% remaining) the colour can already be `#eb562a` / `#ff5a2a` (the 'orange peak' of the pulse). Visually identical to a bomb at fuse=0.8.
Cross-check: visually distinct from the S270 `critical-pulse` spark + the final-0.4s `#ff3030` flash (those still fire only at the end). Concern is purely the mesh tint.
expected: Per the S196 PR body, the mesh tint should stay at the base colour (`#1a1a1a`) for the bulk of the fuse and only lerp to hot orange in the final ~0.6 s. Telegraph value is in the CONTRAST between fresh and about-to-blow bombs — a constant pulse defeats it. Two plausible fixes: (1) only run the pulse when `fuseRemaining < 1.0` (matching the wiggle's 2.0 threshold or a tighter one); (2) anchor the pulse phase to bomb placement time instead of `Date.now()` so a fresh bomb always starts at the grey end.
actual: `bombPulseColor` pulses the mesh between grey and orange on every frame regardless of fuse. The pulse period is `Math.max(0.08, fuseRemaining/8)` — at fuse=2.5 the cycle is 0.31 s; the triangle wave hits orange 50% of the time. A bomb placed at the wrong moment of the global pulse phase shows up bright orange immediately and stays oscillating into orange every 0.15 s. User reads this as 'pool-reused bomb is already red'.
